title: The declared merge order of the topic files
why: RI-DLG01 §A: 'first-match-wins in AUTHORED file order'. Since ARBITRATION S37 the reader
returns the first admissible INFO in that order, so the order is CONTENT: 18.242% of
resolutions across 64 topics move if it moves.
92 of the 468 topic ids are declared in more than one file and hold 488 of the 1,280 INFOs.
For those 38% of the corpus, nobody had ever chosen the order. It was inherited from a
directory listing -- and worse, from TWO DIFFERENT directory listings that disagreed:
* every tool merged in readdirSync().sort() order, i.e. by FILENAME;
* the engine merged in Object.keys(out.topics).sort() order, where the key is
`doc.id || basename` (game/src/engine.js loadData). Three files carry a top-level `id`
(06-opening-roots -> 'opening-roots', 45-speaker-coverage -> 'speaker-coverage',
main-quest-argument -> 'main-quest-argument'), so those files sorted to a DIFFERENT
position in the running game than in every instrument measuring it. 36 of the 92
merged topic ids involve one of them.
So the shipped game and its own instruments were merging the corpus in two different orders,
and under first-match-wins that is two different games. This file ends that: buildTopicIndex()
in game/src/character/converse.js orders the docs by this list and by nothing else, so the
engine, the gate, the census and the lint all read one declared order.
A topic file whose `group` is not listed here is an ERROR, not a file appended at the end.
That is the point: adding a topic file is now a decision about where its INFOs sit relative
to every other file's, and the loader makes you make it.
key: `group` -- the per-file tag buildTopicIndex() already stamps onto every info as `from`. Matched on that, not on the filename, so renaming a file cannot silently change answers.
why_topics_is_empty: This file declares no dialogue. The empty array is load-bearing anyway: several readers in this tree select topic docs with `.filter(d => Array.isArray(d.topics))` (tools/check-dialogue-topics.mjs does), and a manifest without the key is silently dropped by them -- after which buildTopicIndex() sees grouped docs with no manifest and fail-closes, taking a gate every agent runs down with it. That happened once, during the change that added this file. Keep the key.
order_rationale: This list is the FILENAME order the corpus already had, ratified rather than reinvented.
Two reasons, and the second is the one that matters:
70, 75) are themselves an authored statement of order -- somebody numbered these files
to say what comes first. Ratifying that reads the intent that was already there.
2. It is the order every dialogue instrument in the project has been measuring against,
so landing S37 changes the SELECTION RULE and nothing else. Declaring a different order

The three unprefixed files (main-quest-argument, thorn, writ-house) sorted to the end by
accident of the alphabet and are pinned there explicitly. See `open_question` below: that
accident has a known cost and moving it is an authoring decision, deliberately NOT taken here.

open_question.what: `the-steward-of-the-count` is declared by both 50-mainline.json (an old stub) and main-quest-argument.json (authored later, deliberately). Under BOTH the old scoring rule and the new first-match rule, 50-mainline wins, because it comes first -- the W1-17 round-1 hard fail. Promoting main-quest-argument above 50-mainline in this list is now a one-line fix for it.
open_question.why_not_done_here: Resolved by W1-17 builder: the authoritative Act-V argument is intentionally ordered before the legacy mainline stub; provenance gates verify every documented signature.

note_on_counts: `topics` and `infos` are documentation, not law. Nothing reads them; the loader reads `group` and the position. They are here so a reader can see at a glance how much text each position is worth -- the first four files alone hold 220 INFOs and win every tie.
